title: Specter - Embeddings & Rerank Discovery
summary: Discovery to understand Specter's current search stack and requirements for embeddings-based reranking. Customer is exploring Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment for latency-sensitive hybrid search and asking about vector DB integration, throughput at ingest and query time, dimensionality tradeoffs, and security (VPC/KMS/SOC2). Agreed to run benchmark on 1M vectors + hybrid search scenario; Redwood to share pricing and security docs.
topics: vector DB integration patterns (push vs pull)
deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

Jared Kim - send Dedicated vs Hosted cost comparison and pricing tiers - due 2026-07-02

Mike Tran (customer) - provide sample data slice and expected query distribution - due 2026-07-03

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-29 15:00 PDT | Duration 48m | Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Alexa Gomez (Specter CTO), Mike Tran (Specter ML), Sana Iqbal (Product), Omar Reyes (Infra)

[00:00] Jared: All right good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jared from Redwood, this is Priya our solutions engineer. Is this a good time?
[00:07] Alexa: Yeah this works, thanks Jared. We've been looking at embeddings-based reranking for our search product and wanting to understand tradeoffs between hosted and dedicated, especially around latency and throughput.
[00:17] Priya: Great, yeah that's basically our sweet spot. Can you give a quick overview of your current stack and what you want to achieve?
[00:23] Mike: Sure. So right now we run an OpenSearch cluster for ranking with BM25 for recall. We recently added a small FAISS-based service for embeddings for a few premium customers. It's kind of a hybrid setup, right? OpenSearch for keyword recall + FAISS for semantic. The pain is operational complexity and variability in latency under load. Also costs spike when we rescore with cross-encoder models.
[00:45] Jared: OK that's totally common, thanks. What's your current traffic shape and SLA? QPS and P95 latency targets?
[00:52] Sana: Our peak ecom search QPS is roughly 350 QPS, typical query bundle is 70% short tail queries, long tail about 30%. For reranking we want end-to-end p95 under 200ms for the experience tier, and we can tolerate up to 400ms for background / async jobs.
[01:12] Priya: 200ms p95 for rerank is tight but possible; depends on whether you're doing ANN-only rerank or ANN + cross-encoder rescoring. Generally, approximate nearest neighbor (HNSW) on a vector DB gives very low latency for nearest neighbor, but cross-encoder reranking across, say, top-50 candidates will add CPU/GPU time.
[01:30] Mike: Right, our experiments show ANN top-100 recall is ok for discovery, but quality improves with a cross-encoder re-rank on CPU which is slow. We were curious about Redwood's hosting: can you run cross-encoders in the service or do you rely on customers to run those?
[01:45] Priya: We support both patterns. Hosted API can run cross-encoders as part of the request path — you can choose a smaller candidate set from the vector DB then call Redwood to run a cross-encoder rerank. For Dedicated and Private deployments customers often run the ANN and cross-encoder co-located to reduce network hops. We also provide batching and prefix caching to help with throughput.
[02:04] Alexa: How does the vector DB integration look? Push vectors to Redwood or Redwood fetching from your vector DB?
[02:11] Priya: Two common patterns: push model where you compute embeddings in your pipeline and push vectors to a managed vector index (e.g., Pinecone, Milvus) and call Redwood for model scoring, or the reverse where Redwood returns embeddings and you store in your DB. For reranking specifically, many teams use Redwood for embeddings and a vector DB for ANN + Redwood for cross-encoder. Redwood also has connectors and a simple sync agent for private deployments.
[02:33] Omar: Important for us is network topology — we can't have traffic egressing outside our VPC for some PII flows. Is there an on-prem/private option?
[02:40] Jared: Yes, Redwood Private is a VPC/on-prem deployment. We can deploy a private control plane and inference nodes within your network; supports KMS and HSM integrations for key control. Priya, want to add the security bit?
[02:52] Priya: Sure. For Private we support customer-managed VPC peering, SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs and KMS integrations. SOC2 Type II report is available; we'll send the security pack. There can be some additional ops work for private networking but we have templates.
[03:07] Sana: Great. For vector dimensionality our team is debating 128 vs 768 vs 1536. Any guidance on tradeoffs?
[03:14] Priya: Short answer: higher dimensionality usually improves quality for some models but increases storage, indexing and ANN cost. If you're using a transformer embedding at 1536 dims you'll need ~12x storage compared to 128 dims and ANN search latency/throughput will shift. Many customers use 768 as a good compromise. Also quantization (like Q4/Q8) can reduce memory and sometimes slightly affects recall. We'll show you model profiles.
[03:34] Mike: We're using a 768-d embedding from our model today. Current index size is ~120GB for 5M docs. We tried HNSW settings for efConstruction/efSearch; tuning is hard. Does Redwood help with recommended ANN tuning?
[03:46] Priya: Yes, we provide model-to-hardware profiling and recommended HNSW params based on recall targets. For Dedicated we can preconfigure and test the index build parameters. There's also auto-suggest for efSearch vs latency tradeoffs.
[03:58] Alexa: On throughput — for indexing we need to ingest ~10k vectors/second during initial reindex. For queries, peak QPS 350 but not all queries need rerank. How does Redwood handle ingest throughput and backpressure?
[04:10] Jared: For ingest we recommend batching and using our bulk upload API. Hosted accounts have burst capacity but sustained sustained high-throughput indexing often suits Dedicated because you can reserve GPUs/CPU capacity. We also support async upload workers for Private. Priya can talk about batching and KV caching.
[04:24] Priya: Right, continuous batching and async builds reduce pressure. For example, building embedding batches of 1k vectors and streaming writes to vector DB reduces per-call overhead. For Dedicated we can configure instance types and autoscale policy to handle 10k/sec sustained ingest. For Hosted we have quotas and can provision reserved capacity if needed.
[04:40] Omar: For our compliance team we also need audit logs of who accessed what vectors and ability to revoke keys and rotate. How does Redwood expose that?
[04:47] Priya: We emit audit logs for inference calls with token-level metadata; for Private deployments logs can be routed to your SIEM. Key rotation is supported via KMS/ HSM integrations; we don't hold customer plaintext keys in that mode. We'll share the security doc.
[05:02] Mike: A technical question: We use hybrid search now (BM25 + embeddings). We'd like to maintain BM25 for recall and use embeddings to rerank top-k. Any patterns you recommend for latency-conscious rerank?
[05:12] Priya: Yes — common pattern is: 1) query OpenSearch/ES BM25 to get top-N (e.g., top-200), 2) fetch embeddings for those docs from a vector DB or store embeddings in a denormalized store, 3) do ANN or dot-product to re-score quickly, then 4) optionally cross-encoder rerank top-20. If you want p95 under 200ms, aim to minimize network hops and keep candidate set small. Co-locating vector index + cross-encoder (Dedicated/Private) helps.
[05:38] Alexa: For step 2, is it cheaper to store embeddings inside OpenSearch as dense vector fields or keep a separate vector DB?
[05:45] Priya: Both can work. OpenSearch has dense vector fields but indexing and search capabilities differ; many customers use a dedicated vector DB for production for better ANN performance and scaling. If you want unified datastore, OpenSearch or Elastic with vector support is fine for smaller scale. We'll map pros/cons in a doc.
[05:59] Mike: We also run A/B experiments with different embedding models and dimensionality. How does Redwood support model rollouts and versioning?
[06:06] Jared: Redwood supports model versioning and rollouts with canary/A-B policies. In Dedicated you can pin model versions, run canaries on a subset of traffic and automatic fallback if quality degrades. We also integrate eval hooks for prompt sets to detect regression.

[06:26] [10:00] Mike: (inaudible) ... sorry, I lost that one, can you repeat?
[06:31] Priya: No problem — we were talking about rollouts.
[06:33] Mike: OK thanks. Also curious about cost: cross-encoder runs are expensive. Do you have recommendations to minimize unit cost?
[06:40] Priya: Several levers: 1) reduce candidate set size before cross-encoder, 2) quantize models for inference, 3) use Dedicated GPUs to amortize cost for high volume, 4) cache rerank results for hot queries. Redwood Optimize can recommend batching and quantization settings.
[06:55] Alexa: We're also evaluating Pinecone and Milvus. How is Redwood different here — do you compete with vector DBs?
[07:03] Jared: We're not strictly a vector DB — Redwood focuses on model inference and serving, but we integrate with vector DBs. Think of us as the inference/runtime orchestrator that plays nicely with Pinecone/Milvus/OpenSearch. For Dedicated customers we can run both the serving runtime and vector index in the same environment if you prefer.
[07:20] Sana: One more thing: what about approximate vs exact search? For some regulatory customers we need deterministic exact matching for certain fields.
[07:27] Priya: You can do hybrid: exact match for PII-sensitive fields first, then semantic on remaining. For regulated flows, many customers keep exact filters before ANN. We'll add guidance for that.
[07:38] Alexa: Ok can we talk about actual latency numbers? Any benchmarks you can share for 768-d embeddings, HNSW, top-50 ANN and cross-encoder on a single GPU?
[07:48] Priya: Yes — approximate numbers: with 768-d embeddings and a tuned HNSW index, ANN top-50 queries typically return in ~8-20ms on a CPU-optimized vector node. Cross-encoder rerank on a single A10G-class GPU for top-20 can be ~60-120ms depending on batch size and model. Combined end-to-end can be <150ms in Dedicated with co-located infra. Hosted varies based on reservation. We'll provide benchmark spreadsheets.
[08:14] Omar: For Private we need to know network egress patterns. How much traffic flows between vector store and inference nodes?
[08:20] Priya: If co-located, internal network traffic is local; if separate, you'll see per-request fetches for the top-N candidate embeddings — you can mitigate via denormalized caches or by returning embeddings from OpenSearch directly. Also batching reduces round trips.
[08:36] Mike: About benchmarking: we'd like Redwood to run a controlled benchmark against our dataset (1M vectors, 768-d) with hybrid BM25+ANN + cross-encoder. Is that feasible?
[08:45] Jared: Yes that's exactly what we do. Priya will put together a benchmark plan: inputs, QPS target, expected queries, sample data slice. We'll provision test infra (Dedicated mimic) and run Pinecone + OpenSearch + Redwood cross-encoder flows.
[08:58] Priya: We'll need a sample data slice that represents your real distribution and a few golden queries for QA. Also confirm SLOs and which metrics matter: p50/p95/p99, avg cost per 1k queries, recall@k, latency breakdown.
[09:15] Alexa: We'll provide that. A couple quick follow-ups: do you support SAML for SSO and SCIM for auto-provisioning? And how is RBAC surfaced?
[09:23] Priya: Yes SAML SSO and SCIM are supported; RBAC roles for engineers, admins, and billing are available and configurable. In Private you can sync with your IdP.
[09:31] Sana: How about data residency? We have EU customers; can we pin regions?
[09:35] Jared: Hosted supports region selection; Dedicated and Private can be deployed in specific regions or on-prem. We'll note EU region availability.
[09:42] [20:00] Alexa: A bit of a tangent — do you support embedding dimensionality reduction or PCA as a service?
[09:49] Priya: We don't do PCA as a managed pipeline yet; customers often run offline dimension reduction or use smaller embedding models. Redwood Optimize can recommend smaller models or quantization to reduce costs.
[09:59] Mike: Any gotchas for cold-start or warm caches?
[10:03] Priya: Cold caches mean the KV cache isn't primed and your first requests may hit storage; we recommend warm-up jobs. For Dedicated we can set warmup and prefetch policies.
[10:12] Alexa: OK, timeline wise we want to run a pilot in July and then decide on Dedicated vs Hosted. What's reasonable?
[10:20] Jared: That seems reasonable. Pilot in July with benchmark, then decision in ~4 weeks. We'll get pricing and docs over this week.
[10:26] Sana: Are there reference customers doing similar hybrid rerank with Dedicated?
[10:29] Jared: Yes we have a few — we'll include anonymized case studies in the follow-up.
[10:33] Mike: Quick question — you mentioned quantization Q4/Q8. Does Redwood support INT8/GPTQ paths for embedding storage or only for model execution?
[10:41] Priya: We support quantized execution paths for some models (GPTQ/INT8) and also compressed vector storage in vector DBs (like product-quantization). We'll include a compatibility matrix for models and quantization.
[10:52] [30:00] Alexa: (overlap) ... spoken: "...and also can we control fallback logic if the Dedicated nodes are busy?"
[10:59] Jared: We have smart routing and fallback policies — you can route by latency, cost or region and fall back to a cheaper model variant or queue requests. For Hosted our routing will try capacity tiers and fallback to compatible variants.
[11:12] Omar: For Private we need guidance on sizing. Can Redwood provide a starting sizing doc for 350 QPS with 200ms p95 target?
[11:20] Priya: Yes, we'll provide sizing templates and recommended instance types, GPU counts and autoscale rules. We'll model candidate set sizes and cross-encoder throughput.
[11:29] Alexa: Let's recap next steps so nothing falls through:
[11:33] Jared: Sure — recap: Redwood to send pricing (Hosted vs Dedicated) and cost comparison, security and SOC2 docs, benchmarking plan. Specter to provide sample data and golden queries. Priya to draft benchmark infra and run the tests next week. Set follow-up to review results.
[11:49] Alexa: Sounds good. One last thing — any detail on SLA for Dedicated?
[11:53] Jared: Dedicated has an SLA with uptime and latency targets; we'll include the SLA summary in the package.
[11:58] Sana: Thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[12:01] Jared: Thanks all, we'll follow up.

Meeting end.
